milestone: STORAGE-LIFECYCLE-P5C Part 11 -- HOT->COLD automation contract (DESIGN DOCUMENT ONLY)
status: DESIGN ONLY -- NOT IMPLEMENTED, NOT ACTIVATED. No cron entry, supervisord program, or scheduler code was written or modified as part of producing this document.
design_goals: Reuse the already-qualified P5BDeltaReconciler bounded-keyset-batch pattern rather than inventing a new traversal strategy.
Apply the existing 90-day generic HOT retention window boundary already established in the storage lifecycle model.
Preserve permanently pinned rows using the SAME pin-set logic already qualified elsewhere in this project (never re-derive pin criteria ad hoc inside the archival job).
Use the existing single-writer lease mechanism (src/utils/db_locking.py) so this job cannot collide with the 3 live writer services or with itself if triggered twice.

copy-then-verify-before-any-source-retirement semantics: a candidate COLD segment must be built, closed, and identity-verified (row count + digest match against the HOT rows it represents) BEFORE any corresponding HOT row is considered eligible for removal.
Update COLD summaries (transfer_stats_summary/*.summary.json) as part of segment closure so compute_exact_stats_fast() never sees a StaleSummaryError from a freshly-rolled segment.
NEVER touch Watchtower (wt_ops_v2.db) or 3SW2 canonical state under any circumstance -- this job only ever reads and writes transfer_index-shaped data.
NEVER archive or delete rows merely by age without first checking pin status -- age alone is necessary but not sufficient.
Fail closed on any uncertainty: any ambiguous pin-set lookup failure, digest mismatch, or partial-batch error aborts the WHOLE run without touching HOT, not just the ambiguous rows.

proposed_recurring_contract.trigger: Daily cron entry, analogous in form to the existing P2.2 entry, e.g. '0 4 * * * cd .../flex && python3 -m src.ops.hot_cold_archival_runner --once --quiet >> logs/hot_cold_archival.log 2>&1' -- deliberately scheduled at a DIFFERENT hour (04:00) from the existing 03:00 P2.2 cleanup job to avoid any overlap or shared-lock contention between the two independent maintenance jobs.
proposed_recurring_contract.not_yet_created: src/ops/hot_cold_archival_runner.py does not exist. This contract names it only as a design placeholder; creating it is explicitly out of scope for this milestone.
steps: 1. Acquire the single-writer lease (src/utils/db_locking.py) against database/flex_complete_database.db before touching anything. If lease cannot be acquired within a bounded timeout, exit cleanly with pressure_state=SKIPPED_LOCK_CONTENTION and zero rows touched -- never block or retry indefinitely.
2. Compute the 90-day retention boundary id/timestamp against the current HOT table (same boundary logic already qualified in storage_lifecycle_policy.py).
3. Identify candidate rows older than the boundary using a bounded keyset scan (reuse P5BDeltaReconciler's exact batching pattern: fixed batch size, monotonic id cursor, resumable).

4. For each candidate batch: check pin-set membership using the already-established pin-set logic (permanently_pinned_fraction ~15.648% derivation) -- any row that is pinned is excluded from the candidate set for this run, unconditionally, regardless of age.
5. Build (or append to) a COLD segment file for the surviving (non-pinned, aged-out) candidate rows using transfer_cold_store.py's existing segment-building functions.
6. Close the segment and compute its manifest (segment_id, month_covered, row_count, closed_at) -- this is the qualifying step ColdSegmentRegistry already expects.

7. VERIFY before retiring anything: re-read the closed segment file fresh (separate connection), confirm row count and an identity digest over (signature, source, destination, amount_lamports, block_time) match exactly what was selected from HOT in step 3-4. Any mismatch aborts the ENTIRE run without deleting any HOT row, and leaves the just-built COLD segment file quarantined (renamed with a .verify_failed suffix) for human investigation -- never silently discarded, never silently trusted.

8. Only after verification passes: delete the now-archived rows from HOT in the SAME bounded-batch style (never a single unbounded DELETE), inside short transactions to avoid long write locks, releasing the writer lease between batches if the batch count is large.
9. Build the new segment's summary JSON (transfer_stats_summary/<segment_id>.summary.json) via the qualified build_segment_summary() so compute_exact_stats_fast() sees it as fresh immediately.

10. Release the writer lease. Write a run-log record (mirroring storage_lifecycle_runner.py's existing JSON-line log format: run_id, pressure_state, planned/executed/skipped counts, errors, bytes_reclaimed, duration_seconds) to logs/hot_cold_archival.log.
explicit_non_goals_for_this_contract: Does NOT touch database/flex_complete_database.db.p5b_rollback_quarantine in any way.
Does NOT touch wt_ops_v2.db (Watchtower/3SW2 canonical state) in any way.

Does NOT VACUUM the HOT db as part of routine rollover (space reclamation from SQLite page-level deletes is a separate, larger, gated maintenance action -- consistent with the existing project pattern of keeping VACUUM as a distinct manually-gated operation, per the funder_networks archival precedent in project memory).
Does NOT change the P2.2 allowlist cleanup cron's scope.

required_before_this_contract_may_be_act: Unit + integration tests proving: pin-set exclusion is respected under adversarial inputs, copy-then-verify correctly aborts and quarantines on a deliberately corrupted/mismatched segment, bounded batching never holds a write lock beyond a short bounded duration, fail-closed behavior on every identified uncertainty class above.
A dry-run mode (plan-only, zero mutation) exercised against real production HOT data at least once, with its output reviewed by a human before any write-mode run is authorized.
Explicit separate human authorization to install the cron entry and let it run for the first time -- this design document is not that authorization.
qualification_before_activation.note: Per Part 15 of this milestone, activating (or even fully implementing) this contract is NOT required for the cutover itself to be considered healthy -- but per the milestone's explicit retention policy, the rollback DB will be retained until this contract is AT LEAST qualified (implemented + tested), even if not yet activated.
